audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells the player he loses a lane he wins. content.late ends 'This is a losing lane on average' and spikes[3].text ends 'this lane is hard, so you must snowball the L3-4 window or lose.' Darius wins this 55.01% over 958 games. Separately, diff reads FAV while diffRating reads 8.5/10 and both breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t call it hard - that contradiction I did NOT touch, see questionsForUser.
audit.why: cassiopeia's own table carries 44.99%, so the two sides sum to 100.0 and agree Darius is favoured. The chart (Cass L1-2, Darius L3-5, Skill at 6 and first item, Cass at 2+ items) is the exact inverse of cassiopeia's disk chart including every rating, so the chart is mirror-locked and correct - it is only the prose verdict that is wrong.
audit.corrected: You still win this lane on average, so convert the level 3-5 window into a decisive lead.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why and phases[1].why both describe Darius winning ('Your AA + W chop wins most level-1 exchanges', 'your kill threat starts here') under phases whose side is Cassiopeia and whose rating is 2/10. phases[4].why describes only Noxian Guillotine at a stage labelled Skill, and never mentions that Petrifying Gaze arrives on the same level.
audit.why: Noxious Blast is 850 range on a 3.5-second cooldown and grants Cassiopeia Move Speed whenever it hits a champion, which Serpentine Grace then amplifies because 'all Move Speed bonuses are more effective on Cassiopeia'. Apprehend is 535 range and does not exist until level 2. There is no level-1 exchange for Darius to win. At 6 the stage is even because both ultimates land: Petrifying Gaze at 120/100/80 against Noxian Guillotine at 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-2 are hers on range alone; level 6 is even because Petrifying Gaze and Noxian Guillotine arrive together.

audit.whatIsWrong: The one interaction that decides level 6 onward was stated only as a vague instruction to 'approach from an angle' or 'side-angle it'. Petrifying Gaze's real rule is in Riot's own text and is far more actionable than an angle. Twin Fang's two governing properties - its 0.75s cooldown and the fact that it only hits hard on an already-poisoned target, while healing Cassiopeia - appear nowhere on the page, and no field names Grievous Wounds despite the heal.
audit.why: Petrifying Gaze (R, 120/100/80s, 825 range): 'stunning any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slowing any others with their back turned.' Facing is a hard, binary condition Riot states outright - turning your back downgrades a stun to a slow, which is a thing a player can actually execute, unlike 'approach from an angle'. Twin Fang (E, 0.75s, 700 range): 'deals increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt' - so an unpoisoned Cassiopeia is harmless and a poisoned target is on a 0.75-second treadmill she sustains through. Noxious Blast (Q, 3.5s, 850 range) 'grants her increased Move Speed if she hits an enemy champion', and Serpentine Grace makes every one of those speed bonuses larger, so each landed poke also widens the gap you have to close.
audit.corrected: Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing her - turn your back as she casts and it is a slow instead. Twin Fang fires every 0.75s, hits far harder on a poisoned target, and heals her.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Miasma as matchup-defining and gives no number for it, for Petrifying Gaze, or for Apprehend. The two 'Your engage/committal tool' and 'Your ultimate' bullets are placeholders with no content.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 - at rank 1 it is the second-longest non-ultimate cooldown in the lane after Apprehend's 26s, which is what makes the window real rather than theoretical. Petrifying Gaze is 120s at rank 1, the same as Noxian Guillotine.
audit.corrected: Miasma 24s at rank 1, Twin Fang 0.75s but only on poison, Petrifying Gaze 120s, Apprehend 26s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page names Grievous Wounds, despite Twin Fang healing Cassiopeia off every cast against a poisoned target.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/_missing/darius.json flags this matchup as needs-antiheal specifically for Twin Fang. On a 0.75-second cooldown the heal is not incidental - it is her entire sustain model in an extended fight, which is the only kind of fight Darius wants.
audit.corrected: Twin Fang heals her off every tick, so Grievous Wounds is core, not situational.

notes: DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, matching the ruling the mirror audit made from Cassiopeia's side: every string that says Miasma's grounding shuts off Darius's movement or gap-close. Riot's Miasma text is 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities'; Apprehend 'sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him', which is a displacement applied to Cassiopeia rather than movement by Darius, and Noxian Guillotine 'leaps to an enemy champion'. Whether grounding stops either is exactly the class of thing champ-data marks unknown, so I did not assert it in any direction and I did not delete the existing claims. On this page it survives in spikes[0].text, the mid text and whys[1]; I rewrote late in a way that states what Miasma does without claiming what it stops. The kit file's derived flag on Darius's E reads 'knockup', which Riot's Apprehend text does not support - it says only that he pulls enemies to him - so no field here calls it a knock-up.
